safety_lead_time.comparison_action: reduce SAP safety lead time from 4.0 to 0.89 days

narrative: Material PL1__MC705553 shows variable but largely continuous demand (CV=49.5%, 95.7% active working days) over the observation window with a detected declining trend. Lead times are very short (effective mean ~1.02 days) after trimming one extreme 19.17-day outlier. A continuous-review (r,Q) policy is recommended with safety stock of 296 units providing 95% service level coverage. The EOQ of 5,128 units is capped to 3,817 units by the 4,114-unit storage limit, representing a binding capacity constraint that should be reviewed to unlock full cost optimisation.
warnings: Storage capacity is binding: EOQ 5128 units capped to 3817 units (max_storage_units - safety_stock = 3817.95)
Extreme lead-time outlier detected: 19.17 days (next highest: 5.0). Trimmed from effective lead time calculation.
SAP safety stock is 0 — current policy provides no buffer against demand/lead-time variability.
SAP safety lead time of 4.0 days is excessive vs. effective lead time of 1.02 days; recommend reduction to 0.89 days.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is variable but largely continuous (95.7% non-zero days, CV=49.5%), making a continuous-review reorder-point model appropriate. The short, stable lead time (1 day effective) suits a fixed-order-quantity trigger rather than periodic review. EOQ minimises ordering vs. holding cost trade-off subject to the MOQ=500 and storage cap constraints.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage cap of 4,113.95 units reduces order quantity from EOQ 5,128 to 3,817 units, increasing ordering frequency and annual ordering cost by ~34%. If demand grows, the cap will become increasingly restrictive and service level protection may erode.
research_insights.escalation_flag: none — MOQ (500) + safety stock (296) = 796 units, well below max_storage_units (4,114). No MOQ-capacity infeasibility.
